say.en: Iron ore is mined in Odisha, made into steel in Jamshedpur, shaped into a bicycle in Ludhiana, and bought in a shop in Bengaluru. Each step is a different kind of business. In this lesson: Classify industries as primary, secondary and tertiary.
Explain the meaning of commerce as trade and auxiliaries to trade.

body.en: *Industry* is the part of business concerned with producing or processing goods. Primary industries obtain goods from nature: extractive (mining, fishing, forestry) and genetic (breeding plants and animals, nurseries, poultry). Secondary industries process raw materials into finished goods: manufacturing (analytical, synthetical, processing, assembling) and construction (buildings, roads, dams). Tertiary industries provide supporting services such as transport, banking, insurance, warehousing, communication and advertising, which are also called auxiliaries to trade.

say.en: Commerce includes all activities that bring goods from producers to consumers.
Trade: buying and selling, internal or external.
Transport removes the hindrance of place.
Warehousing removes the hindrance of time.
Banking removes the hindrance of finance.

Advertising removes the hindrance of information.
Communication removes the hindrance of distance in contact.

title.en: Commerce and the hindrances it removes

body.en: *Commerce* consists of trade and the auxiliaries to trade. Trade (internal or external) removes the hindrance of persons, bringing buyer and seller together. Transport removes the hindrance of place, warehousing the hindrance of time, banking the hindrance of finance, insurance the hindrance of risk, advertising the hindrance of information, and communication the hindrance of contact at a distance. Together, industry makes goods and commerce makes them available where and when they are wanted.

problem.en: Trace the business activities involved in getting a cotton shirt to a customer and classify each.

steps.en: Growing cotton on a farm: primary (genetic) industry.
Spinning, weaving and stitching: secondary (manufacturing) industry.
Transporting, storing, financing and insuring the shirts: tertiary (auxiliaries).
Wholesalers and retailers selling the shirts: trade.

Transporting, storing, financing and insuring the shirts: tertiary auxiliaries.
Wholesalers and retailers selling the shirts: trade.
So the answer is Primary gives secondary gives tertiary services gives trade.
